facts.statement: Without prior consent, telemarketing calls to a residence are allowed only between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. at the called person's location.
facts.quote: at any time other than between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. local time at the called person's location

items.stem: Without prior consent, the Telemarketing Sales Rule allows outbound sales calls to a person's residence only between:
options: 7 a.m. and 10 p.m., the caller's local time
8 a.m. and 9 p.m., the caller's local time
8 a.m. and 9 p.m., the called person's local time
9 a.m. and 8 p.m., the called person's local time
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.4(c) bars outbound telemarketing calls to a residence, without prior consent, at any time other than 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. local time at the called person's location.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: A seller may call a number on the do-not-call registry if it has an established business relationship with the person, who has not asked the seller not to call.
facts.quote: (2) Can demonstrate that the seller has an established business relationship with such person

items.stem: A producer wants to call a prospect whose number is on the national do-not-call registry. Which of the following would allow the sales call?
options: The number appears in a public phone directory
The producer is licensed in the prospect's state
The call is made by an automated system
The prospect bought a policy from the producer last year
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.4(b)(1)(iii)(B) permits a call to a registered number when the seller has an established business relationship with the person, such as a purchase within the past 540 days, and the person has not asked the seller not to call.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: A seller may also call a registered number with the person's express written agreement to receive its calls.
facts.quote: Can demonstrate that the seller has obtained the express agreement, in writing, of such person to place calls to that person

items.stem: Besides an established business relationship, which of the following allows a seller to make sales calls to a number on the national do-not-call registry?
options: The person's verbal agreement given to a lead vendor
A referral from one of the person's friends
The person's express written agreement to receive its calls
Purchase of the number from a licensed list broker
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.4(b)(1)(iii)(B) allows calls to a registered number if the seller has the person's express agreement, in writing, including the number and the person's signature.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: A person who has told the seller not to call may not be called by that seller.
facts.quote: (A) That person previously has stated that he or she does not wish to receive an outbound telephone call made by or on behalf of the seller

items.stem: A customer who bought a policy from an agency last year tells the agency to stop calling her. Her number is not on the national registry. May the agency keep calling her with sales offers?
options: Yes, because her number is not on the registry
Yes, because of the established business relationship
Yes, but only between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m.
No, because of her request to that seller
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.4(b)(1)(iii)(A) prohibits calling a person who has stated she does not wish to receive calls from that seller, whether or not she is on the registry and despite any business relationship.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: An established business relationship based on a purchase lasts 540 days.
facts.quote: within the 540 days immediately preceding the date of a telemarketing call

items.stem: Under the Telemarketing Sales Rule, an established business relationship based on a person's purchase from the seller lasts for how many days after the purchase?
options: 90 days
180 days
365 days
540 days
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.2 defines an established business relationship to include a purchase or financial transaction within the 540 days before the call.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: An established business relationship based on an inquiry or application lasts 90 days.
facts.quote: within the 90 days immediately preceding the date of a telemarketing call

items.stem: A prospect asked an agency about a policy but did not buy. Under the Telemarketing Sales Rule, the established business relationship created by that inquiry lasts:
options: 30 days
90 days
180 days
540 days
items.explanation: 16 C.F.R. § 310.2 treats an inquiry or application as creating an established business relationship for the 90 days before a call.
items.retired: Sourced to the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule, which largely does not reach state-regulated insurance. Replaced by items sourced to the FCC's TCPA rules (47 C.F.R. 64.1200).

facts.statement: No telephone solicitation may be made to a residence before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m., local time at the called party's location.
facts.quote: before the hour of 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (local time at the called party's location)

items.stem: Under the federal telemarketing rules that apply to insurance sales calls, a producer may make a telephone solicitation to a residence only between:
options: 7 a.m. and 10 p.m., the caller's local time
8 a.m. and 9 p.m., the caller's local time
8 a.m. and 9 p.m., the called party's local time
9 a.m. and 8 p.m., the called party's local time
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(c) bars telephone solicitations to a residential subscriber before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m., local time at the called party's location.

items.stem: A New Jersey producer wants to make a sales call at 6:30 p.m. Eastern time to a prospect at home in California, where it is 3:30 p.m. Under the federal calling-hour rule, the call is:
options: Prohibited, because it is after 6 p.m. for the caller
Prohibited, because interstate sales calls need written consent
Permitted only with a recorded disclosure at the start
Permitted, because it is 3:30 p.m. where the prospect is
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(c) measures the 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. window by local time at the called party's location. 3:30 p.m. in California is within it.

facts.statement: A call to a person with whom the caller has an established business relationship is not a telephone solicitation under the do-not-call rules.
facts.quote: (ii) To any person with whom the caller has an established business relationship

items.stem: A producer wants to call a prospect whose number is on the national do-not-call registry. Which of the following allows the sales call?
options: The prospect's number is already in the agency's database
The prospect's neighbor referred the agency 2 months ago
The prospect visited the agency's website 6 months ago
The prospect bought a policy from the agency 10 months ago
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(f)(15) excludes from telephone solicitation a call to a person with whom the caller has an established business relationship, such as a purchase within the past 18 months.

facts.statement: A call made with the person's prior express invitation or permission is not a telephone solicitation.
facts.quote: (i) To any person with that person's prior express invitation or permission

items.stem: Besides an established business relationship, which of the following takes a sales call outside the federal do-not-call restrictions?
options: A referral from one of the person's friends
Purchase of the number from a licensed list broker
The person's listing in a professional directory
The person told the agency beforehand that it may call
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(f)(15) excludes from telephone solicitation any call to a person who gave prior express invitation or permission.
items.retired: The national registry exception requires signed, written permission (47 C.F.R. 64.1200(c)(2)), which the sourced excerpt does not show. Withheld until that paragraph is sourced.

facts.statement: An established business relationship based on a purchase or transaction lasts 18 months.
facts.quote: within the eighteen (18) months immediately preceding the date of the telephone call

items.stem: Under the federal do-not-call rules, an established business relationship based on a client's purchase lasts for how long after the purchase?
options: 3 months
6 months
12 months
18 months
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(f) bases an established business relationship on a purchase or transaction within the 18 months before the call.

items.stem: A client bought a single-premium policy from an agency 20 months ago and has had no other dealings with it since. Her number is on the national do-not-call registry. May the agency make a sales call to her?
options: Yes, because she is a past customer
Yes, because registrations expire after five years
Yes, as long as the call is made before 9 p.m.
No, because the 18-month business relationship has ended
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(f) bases an established business relationship on a purchase or transaction within the 18 months before the call. At 20 months with no further dealings, it has ended, so the registry applies.

facts.statement: An established business relationship based on an inquiry or application lasts three months.
facts.quote: within the three months immediately preceding the date of the call

items.stem: A prospect asked an agency about a life policy but did not buy. Under the federal do-not-call rules, the established business relationship from that inquiry lasts:
options: 30 days
3 months
6 months
18 months
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(f) bases an established business relationship on an inquiry or application within the three months before the call.

facts.statement: A company must honor a consumer's do-not-call request within a reasonable time, not more than 10 business days.
facts.quote: This period may not exceed ten (10) business days from the receipt of such request.

items.stem: A customer asks an agency to put her on its internal do-not-call list. Under federal rules, the agency must honor the request within a reasonable time that may not exceed:
options: 24 hours
5 business days
10 business days
30 days
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(d)(3) requires honoring a do-not-call request within a reasonable time, not to exceed 10 business days from receipt.
items.retired: The FCC shortened this period from 30 days to 10 business days in 2024; prep materials and possibly the exam bank still teach 30 days, so a candidate could be marked wrong for the current rule. Withheld until the exam's content is confirmed.

facts.statement: National do-not-call registrations must be honored indefinitely, until cancelled by the consumer or removed by the administrator.
facts.quote: Such do-not-call registrations must be honored indefinitely, or until the registration is cancelled by the consumer or the telephone number is removed by the database administrator.

items.stem: A consumer put her number on the national do-not-call registry six years ago and has done nothing since. What is the status of her registration?
options: It expired after five years
It must be renewed before it is honored
It covers only calls from in-state sellers
It is still in effect
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(c) requires national registrations to be honored indefinitely, until the consumer cancels them or the administrator removes the number.

facts.statement: When a consumer asks not to be called, the caller must record the request and add the number to its do-not-call list at the time of the request.
facts.quote: the person or entity must record the request and place the subscriber's name, if provided, and telephone number on the do-not-call list at the time the request is made

items.stem: A client who bought a policy from an agency last year tells the producer on a call, "Please don't call me with sales offers anymore." Her number is not on the national registry. What must the agency do?
options: Keep calling until her number appears on the national registry
Log the request and put her number on its internal list
Stop only the producer she spoke with from calling
Wait for her written confirmation before changing anything
items.explanation: 47 C.F.R. § 64.1200(d)(3) requires a caller that receives a do-not-call request to record it and place the number on its do-not-call list at the time the request is made.
